extraction.name: ScienceQA
extraction.description: ScienceQA is a large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question answering dataset containing 21,208 examples collected from elementary and high school science curricula. It covers three subjects (natural science, social science, and language science) across 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills. Most questions are annotated with lectures (general background knowledge) and explanations (specific reasoning for the answer), making it suitable for studying chain-of-thought reasoning in AI systems.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from elementary and high school science curricula. Questions are annotated with lectures and explanations. The dataset was split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Elementary and high school science curricula, covering natural science, social science, and language science topics.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20. Each split has 12,726, 4,241, and 4,241 examples, respectively. Images were converted to captions using a captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 for use as visual context in language models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The lecture provides general knowledge that introduces the background information for solving problems of a similar class. The explanation reveals a specific reason for the answer. 83.9% of questions are annotated with a lecture and 90.5% with an explanation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for human performance evaluation only)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human performance evaluation, each question was answered by three different workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers were required to have a high school or higher degree and pass qualification examples.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Workers required to have a high school or higher degree and pass qualification examples.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ViT and GPT-2 based captioning model (for image-to-caption conversion)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal methods fail to achieve satisfactory performance on ScienceQA. There is a 20.07% gap between human performance and the best model for questions with image context. Models fail to understand multimodal inputs and lack domain-specific knowledge, or generate wrong chains of thought with irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of multimodal question answering models; benchmarking multi-hop reasoning ability and interpretability of AI systems; studying chain-of-thought reasoning in language models; few-shot and fine-tuning learning experiments.

name.evidence: we present Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA), a new benchmark that consists of 21k multimodal multiple choice questions with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations.

description.evidence: SCIENCE QA is collected from elementary and high school science curricula, and contains 21,208 examples along with lectures and explanations. Different from existing datasets, SCIENCE QA has richer domain diversity from three different subjects: natural science, social science, and language science.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We randomly split the dataset into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20. Each split has 12,726, 4,241, and 4,241 examples, respectively. We extract the caption from the captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 for the image as the visual context.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We post the task to Amazon Mechanical Turk and ask workers to answer SCIENCE QA questions. Only workers who obtain a high school or higher degree and pass the qualification examples are qualified for the study.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Each worker needs to answer a set of 10 test questions, and each question is answered by three different workers.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We extract the caption from the captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 for the image as the visual context.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Humans outperform all benchmarks consistently across question classes, context types, and grades, e.g., a 20.07% gap for questions with the image context (IMG) between humans and our best performing model. The failure cases can be classified into two types: (a) the model fails to understand the multimodal inputs and lacks domain-specific knowledge to arrive at the correct answer; (b) the model generates the wrong chain of thought with irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete information.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we present Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA), a new benchmark that consists of 21k multimodal multiple choice questions with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. We further design language models to learn to generate lectures and explanations as the chain of thought (CoT) to mimic the multi-hop reasoning process when answering SCIENCE QA questions.
